tools.name: list_networks
tools.description: The 16 networks in Multimedia Monster's scope. Each has a status (live: real posts sent from Multimedia Monster's server; planned: not posting yet) and its routes (official_api, webhook or browser) with how far each is built. Optional filters: status, route.

tools.name: get_requirements
tools.description: For one network (or all): the account type the network requires, how the brand grants Multimedia Monster access, the minimum role Multimedia Monster accepts and what it never accepts, and whether the network verifies the business; plus the requirements common to every network and the acts only the b

tools.name: get_onboarding_steps
tools.description: How a brand is onboarded, step by step: what the brand receives, what the brand does and what Multimedia Monster does at each stage, what the brand provides, and how to start.

tools.name: request_quote
tools.description: Records a quote request for Multimedia Monster; it answers at the contact email. Returns a request id only: no price is returned (pricing is by quote, set by Multimedia Monster). Required: company, contact_email. Optional: contact_name, website, networks (codes from list_networks), services, message

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_offer, list_networks · Private data: request_quote · Public sink: get_offer, list_networks, request_quote.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_offer, list_networks · Private data: request_quote · Public sink: get_offer, list_networks, request_quote

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
